name: Opus Picks-and-Shovels
strategy: A two-leg bet on the AI-buildout memory bottleneck (Micron in DRAM/HBM, Sandisk in NAND) kept at its pre-stop size, with the stopped-out Lam Research wafer-fab-equipment leg left in 4% cash rather than re-bought into a rate-hike-driven chip tape.
reassessment_note: Research this week (web search plus a fetched TradingKey/Goldman write-up) shows the 10-14 to 10-16 drop was driven by two things. The first is China's CXMT claiming progress on 4F2 DRAM, which Goldman models as capacity rising from 290k to 513k wafers/month by end-2028 but still meeting only about 50% of China's DRAM demand, and it says the market overestimates the technology risk. The second is a hot September CPI (0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y) that revived Fed-hike bets and pushed the 10-year above 5.3%. Neither breaks the near-term thesis: KeyBanc still projects Q4 DRAM contract prices +15-20% q/q and NAND about +20%, and Micron says its HBM is sold out through 2027 and has 26 strategic customer agreements. So I am keeping the memory legs and re-underwriting them at the 10-19 close. I accept that this resets MU's stop, which sat only about 0.7% below the 10-16 mark. That is a deliberate re-underwrite, not a way to dodge the stop: the new 16% stop still caps a further loss of about 7% of NAV on MU. What did change: the rate regime is hostile to high-beta semis, and the WFE leg was stopped out. I am not chasing LRCX back, even though TSMC kept its $60-64B capex guide. Its 21% stays in cash at 4% until the hike path is clearer. Gross exposure falls from 90% to 67%.

positions.thesis: Micron fell about 13% on the week on a CXMT supply fear that Goldman dates to 2027-28 capacity, while the near-term setup is the strongest in the cycle: Q4 DRAM contracts are guided +15-20% q/q, HBM is guided +80-100% q/q into Q1 2027 and sold out through 2027, and strategic agreements rose from 16 to 26. Holding 45% keeps this as the book's core bottleneck claim. The 16% stop from the 10-19 entry bounds the downside if the market is right that the 2028 downcycle is coming early.

Sandisk is the NAND half of the memory squeeze. NAND contract pricing is guided about +20%, and enterprise SSD demand is being pulled by AI inference storage. It fell about 15% on the week on a DRAM-specific CXMT headline that does not directly touch NAND supply. I trimmed it slightly from 24% to 22% because it is the higher-beta name in a rising-rate tape. The 20% stop allows for its larger daily moves.
